statements.text: So, Mr. Sherman, how are you leveraging AI-backed technologies to discover and remediate vulnerabilities before adversaries can exploit them?
statements.context: House Armed Services Committee hearing on AI, IT, and DOD network security.

statements.text: How is the Air Force thinking about resourcing for the autonomy/AI Pilot on an aircraft platform, as part of a program budget? [...] Does that percentage for CCA's match the percentage of funding for autonomy capability needs in other programs? [...] General Brown. The Department of the Air Force (DAF) is investing heavily in Collaborative Combat Aircraft (CCA) Research, Development, Technology, and Evaluation (RDT&E) as a critical step in delivering effective combat mass in highly contested environments [...] reflecting the DAF's sense of urgency to outpace our competitors in pursuing these technologies.
statements.context: Written exchange submitted for the record during a House Armed Services Committee hearing on the Department of the Air Force Fiscal Year 2024 budget request.

statements.text: The FY24 President's Budget requests $394M for autonomous platform development, $68M for autonomy development through Project VENOM, and $72M to solve Doctrine, Organization, Training, Materiel, Leadership and Education, Personnel, Facilities and Policy solutions by standing up an Experimental Operations Unit.
statements.context: House Armed Services Committee hearing on the Department of the Air Force FY2024 budget request, where Representative Fallon questions Secretary Kendall on autonomy/AI funding for the Collaborative Combat Aircraft program.
